notes.meaning: Christ compares Himself to a sweet rose and a lowly lily, showing His beauty and how easily His people can approach Him. He comes into our world not with terrifying majesty, but with gentle sweetness and grace. In Him, believers find everything delightful and refreshing to the soul.

The bridegroom answers by declaring that his beloved outshines all other maidens just as a delicate lily surpasses jagged thorns. In the traditional view, Christ looks upon His church as precious, pure, and uniquely chosen. Though believers live in a world filled with hurtful and ungodly influences, Christ keeps and values them above all else.

The bride compares her lover to a fruitful apple tree that stands out among the barren trees of the forest. Spiritually, believers find that Christ excels all other beings, offering a safe and refreshing shade from the scorching heat of life. Resting under His care, the soul feasts on sweet blessings such as pardon, peace, and grace.

The lover brings his bride into his banquet hall, openly displaying his love as a royal banner. Spiritually, Christ leads the believer into deep fellowship with Himself, welcoming the soul into His house to enjoy the rich feast of the gospel. His public mark over His people is not anger or fear, but steadfast, protecting love.

The bride cries out for raisin cakes and fresh apples to revive her because she is overwhelmed by the power of love. In Christian experience, the soul that tastes the deep love of Christ can feel overcome with joy and longing. Believers look to the sustaining promises of God's Word to strengthen and support them in these times.

The bridegroom places his left hand under her head to support her while his right arm holds her close. This picture shows the tender and complete care Christ gives to those who depend on Him. In times of weakness, both His quiet daily care and His mighty saving grace hold believers secure so they cannot fall.

The bride solemnly urges the young women of Jerusalem not to stir up or interrupt love until the right moment. Spiritually, this warns believers to be watchful and careful in their walk with God. True communion with Christ is a delicate blessing that should never be disturbed by sin, impatience, or careless living.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars read this as a warning not to stir up romantic love in yourself before its right time, when God awakens it.

notes.meaning: The bride suddenly hears the voice of her beloved and sees him leaping joyfully over the hills to reach her. Traditionally, this shows Christ coming swiftly to rescue and comfort His church. No mountain of difficulty, guilt, or human weakness can hold Him back from drawing near to His people.

The lover is compared to a swift, graceful deer who stands near the wall and looks through the window lattice. Spiritually, this illustrates how Christ stays very close to His people even when they cannot see Him fully. In this life, believers catch sweet glimpses of His grace as through a screen, knowing He watches over them with love.

The bridegroom speaks directly to his beloved, urging her to rise up and come away with him. In the same way, Christ calls to the soul with words of grace and warmth. He invites believers to leave behind their spiritual laziness and worldliness to walk with Him in close fellowship.

The lover reminds his bride that the cold winter rains have ended and pleasant days have arrived. In a spiritual sense, this describes how the cold darkness of guilt and fear passes away when Christ comes. His presence drives away the storm of sin and brings the warmth of God's favor.

New flowers bloom across the earth, birds begin to sing, and the gentle voice of the turtledove echoes through the land. This points to the joyful arrival of the gospel, which brings new spiritual life after a long spiritual winter. Where God's grace takes root, mourning turns into songs of thanksgiving and praise.

The fig tree begins to ripen its sweet fruit and the grapevines fill the air with their fragrance, prompting another tender call to come away. Christ points His followers to the budding fruits of His grace as a reason to draw near. He persistently calls His people to step out in faith and share in His life.

The lover addresses his bride as a shy dove hiding in the clefts of the high rocks, asking to see her face and hear her voice. Spiritually, the church finds safety hidden in Christ, the solid Rock of salvation. Even when believers feel weak or fearful, Christ assures them that their prayers are sweet and their presence is precious to Him.

A command is given to capture the little foxes that creep into the vineyards and damage the blooming vines. In the Christian life, this warns believers to catch small sins, bad habits, and harmful teachings early before they grow. Guarding the heart against little compromises protects our love and devotion to God.

The bride expresses joyful assurance that she belongs entirely to her beloved, and he belongs to her. Spiritually, this highlights the unshakable covenant bond between Christ and His church. Believers take comfort knowing they are His forever, and that He delights to dwell and shepherd among His pure-hearted people.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: In Catholic devotion, Mary is honored as the "mystical rose" and often pictured with a lily, as the lily without equal among God's holy people.

notes.meaning: The bride asks her beloved to return quickly like a swift deer across the rugged mountains until the dawn breaks and the shadows flee. For the church, this is a prayer for Christ's constant presence and help throughout the dark trials of this world. Believers look forward to the eternal morning of the resurrection, when all darkness and sorrow will disappear forever.
